doc.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Teaching at Lehman and Juilliard
summary: Stewart retired from the Board of Education, runs the Lehman jazz program, and teaches jazz history at Juilliard.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Are you still — you said you retired from teaching just recently?

I retired from the Board of Education in New York. You know I did 25 years so I retired from that, but I’m still teaching and I run the jazz program up at Lehman College as well as I teach jazz history at Juilliard, one semester a year, which is plenty, it’s enough. And it leaves me time to practice, tour, or do whatever I need to do.
Yeah. Is it hard to teach the history of jazz in one semester?
Time, I mean like to give credit due.

Yes, very difficult. Because most of the time, even if you teach from 1900 to 1950 in one semester it’s difficult because you spend most of my time figuring out who to leave out. You know what I mean? Just who do I — because you can’t tell them about it because there’s no way they’re going to remember if I start laying all the names on them and everything. So I try and pick key people so that they remember, you know but I also put out a disclaimer when I say listen, now when you go to your friends or your friend who’s a jazz fan and you say well I learned about this and this and this, and they say to you well what about such and so and such? And you say well he didn’t tell us about him. I said I’m telling you now, that’s going to happen. Because there’s no way I can tell you about everybody and hope that you will remember anybody. So I’m trying to tell you about certain people and deal with that rather than give too many names to you and you don’t remember anything.
